spec.description: Up/down status, request rate/latency, and worker queue health for every service added by the observability migration - the dashboard the infra-health alert rules (services/grafana/provisioning/alerting/rules.yml) are conceptually about.

spec.title: MCP dev
spec.description:
Goal: quickly see if the mcp-dev MCP service is up.
Description: combines the Prometheus `up` scrape result for job mcp-dev with the blackbox exporter's HTTP health-check probe for that instance into a single UP/DOWN stat.

spec.title: MCP stats
spec.description:
Goal: quickly see if the mcp-stats MCP service is up.
Description: combines the Prometheus `up` scrape result for job mcp-stats with the blackbox exporter's HTTP health-check probe for that instance into a single UP/DOWN stat, mirroring the "mcp-stats is down" alert rule's own query.

spec.title: Scrape targets
spec.description: up{} across every Prometheus scrape job - one row per exporter/service the observability stack itself depends on to see anything at all.

spec.title: Firing alerts
spec.description: Grafana-managed alert rules (services/grafana/provisioning/alerting/rules.yml) currently firing, pending, or erroring.

spec.title: Blackbox exporter
spec.description: All blackbox probe-scrape series share one exporter process - if any go to 0 together, the exporter itself is unreachable, not just one probed target.

spec.title: Prometheus
spec.description: Self-scrape - if this goes stale/DOWN, every other panel on this dashboard is suspect too.

spec.title: Memory fragmentation ratio
spec.description: RSS/used-memory ratio - sustained values well above 1 mean the OS is holding memory Redis isn't using (fragmentation); below 1 can mean swapping.

spec.title: Request rate
spec.description:
Goal: track HTTP request throughput for the mcp-dev service.
Description: sums the rate of http_requests_total over 5m windows for the mcp-dev instance, grouped by handler.

spec.title: Latency (p50/p90/p95)
spec.description:
Goal: track HTTP request latency percentiles for the mcp-dev service.
Description: histogram_quantile over http_request_duration_seconds_bucket for the mcp-dev instance at the 0.50/0.90/0.95 quantiles, grouped by handler.

spec.title: Request rate
spec.description:
Goal: track HTTP request throughput for the mcp-stats service.
Description: sums the rate of http_requests_total over 5m windows for the mcp-stats instance, grouped by handler.

spec.title: Latency (p50/p90/p95)
spec.description:
Goal: track HTTP request latency percentiles for the mcp-stats service.
Description: histogram_quantile over http_request_duration_seconds_bucket for the mcp-stats instance at the 0.50/0.90/0.95 quantiles, grouped by handler.

spec.title: Access log
spec.description:
Goal: let engineers inspect raw nginx access log lines from the load balancer to debug routing/backend selection issues.
Description: streams Loki log lines from the load-balancer container's stdout stream, filtered to the backend(s) selected via the $backend dashboard variable.

spec.title: Error log
spec.description:
Goal: let engineers inspect raw nginx error log lines from the load balancer to debug worker/upstream failures.
Description: streams Loki log lines from the load-balancer container's stderr stream. nginx's error_log directive can't log a $backend_name variable like access_log does, so Alloy instead derives a best-effort backend label from the port in the line's own "host:" field (absent on lines with no request context, e.g. worker-level errors) - no $backend filter here since it's inferred, not logged directly.

spec.title: Claude
spec.description:
Goal: let engineers glance at whether any Claude traffic has fallen back from litellm to the real api.anthropic.com, without hunting through Load balancer log tabs.
Description: counts access-log lines on the anthropic-wire proxy port (4001) tagged backend=anthropic-proxy-fallback over the dashboard's time range - nonzero means litellm didn't respond and a request was served by the real provider instead.

spec.title: Codex
spec.description:
Goal: let engineers glance at whether any Codex/OpenAI traffic has fallen back from litellm to the real api.openai.com, without hunting through Load balancer log tabs.
Description: counts access-log lines on the openai-wire proxy port (4002) tagged backend=openai-proxy-fallback over the dashboard's time range - nonzero means litellm didn't respond and a request was served by the real provider instead.

spec.title: Provider fallback
spec.description:
Goal: let engineers drill into who got redirected to the real Anthropic/OpenAI provider, to which provider, and when, once the top-level Claude/Codex fallback cards show nonzero.
Description: streams Loki log lines from the load-balancer container's stdout stream, filtered to the anthropic-proxy-fallback and openai-proxy-fallback backends only.

spec.title: Recent LiteLLM alerts
spec.description:
Goal: surface LiteLLM's own budget/outage/exception/hang signals (things our generic_api StandardLoggingPayload callback cannot reconstruct) as soon as they fire.
Description: lists the most recent 100 litellm_alerts rows newest first, with event as a visible sortable column so a viewer can scan/filter by alert type; raw_payload (full JSON, shape varies per alert type) is shown via the inspect drawer rather than a fixed-width column.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT received_at, event, event_group, key_alias, team_id, user_id, spend, max_budget, event_message, raw_payload
FROM litellm_alerts
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at)
ORDER BY received_at DESC
LIMIT 100

spec.title: Error rate by model over time
spec.description:
Goal: spot which model is driving up API-level failures right now, not just the aggregate error rate.
Description: joins agent_events to agent_usage on litellm_call_id (unique per call) to attach a model to each event, buckets into 5-minute intervals, and computes failures / total calls per model per bucket.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(e.timestamp, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  u.model AS metric,
  countIf(e.status = 'failure') / nullIf(count(), 0) AS value
FROM agent_events e
INNER JOIN agent_usage u ON e.litellm_call_id = u.litellm_call_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.timestamp)
  AND e.litellm_call_id != ''
GROUP BY time, metric
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Error rate by provider over time
spec.description:
Goal: tell whether a spike in failures is provider-wide (an upstream outage) or isolated to one model within a provider.
Description: same join/bucketing as "Error rate by model over time" but grouped by agent_usage.provider (claude/openai/other) instead of the individual model.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(e.timestamp, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  u.provider AS metric,
  countIf(e.status = 'failure') / nullIf(count(), 0) AS value
FROM agent_events e
INNER JOIN agent_usage u ON e.litellm_call_id = u.litellm_call_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.timestamp)
  AND e.litellm_call_id != ''
GROUP BY time, metric
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Latency p95 by model over time
spec.description:
Goal: see whether one model is dragging p95 latency up, since a slow-but-rare model can hide inside an all-model average.
Description: joins agent_events to agent_usage on litellm_call_id to attach a model to each call, buckets into 5-minute intervals, and computes quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) per model per bucket.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(e.timestamp, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  u.model AS metric,
  quantile(0.95)(e.latency_ms) AS value
FROM agent_events e
INNER JOIN agent_usage u ON e.litellm_call_id = u.litellm_call_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.timestamp)
  AND e.litellm_call_id != ''
  AND e.latency_ms IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY time, metric
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Latency p99 by model over time
spec.description:
Goal: catch tail-latency outliers per model that p95 alone can smooth over.
Description: same join/bucketing as the p95 panel, computing quantile(0.99)(latency_ms) per model per bucket instead.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(e.timestamp, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  u.model AS metric,
  quantile(0.99)(e.latency_ms) AS value
FROM agent_events e
INNER JOIN agent_usage u ON e.litellm_call_id = u.litellm_call_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.timestamp)
  AND e.litellm_call_id != ''
  AND e.latency_ms IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY time, metric
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Spend trend (cost over time)
spec.description:
Goal: watch overall spend trend so a budget alert (see litellm_alerts row above) can be read against the spend that actually caused it.
Description: buckets agent_usage into 5-minute intervals and sums LiteLLM-reported cost per bucket - no local pricing math, cost comes straight from LiteLLM's own response_cost - and overlays a second series counting litellm_alerts rows per bucket whose event looks budget/threshold-related, so a spend spike can be read against when a budget alert actually fired.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(timestamp, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  sum(cost) AS value
FROM agent_usage
WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

SELECT
  toStartOfInterval(received_at, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time,
  count() AS budget_alerts
FROM litellm_alerts
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at)
  AND (positionCaseInsensitive(event, 'budget') > 0 OR positionCaseInsensitive(event, 'threshold') > 0)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

spec.title: Ingest DLQ row count
spec.description:
Goal: give the unresolved ingest_dlq dead-letter feed an at-a-glance signal that something still needs triage.
Description: counts ingest_dlq_unresolved rows (rejected agent_events/agent_usage/etc. inserts not yet marked resolved) in the selected time range - any non-zero value means unreplayed failures still need attention.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count() AS dlq_count
FROM ingest_dlq_unresolved
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at)

spec.title: Ingest DLQ recent rows
spec.description:
Goal: give the unresolved ingest_dlq dead-letter feed an actual triage view instead of sitting write-only.
Description: lists the most recent 100 ingest_dlq_unresolved rows (which target table rejected the insert, the error, and the offending litellm_call_id/session_id/raw_row, not yet marked resolved) ordered newest first; raw_row is the full JSON of the rejected row, shown via the inspect drawer rather than a fixed-width column.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT occurred_at, stage, litellm_call_id, session_id, error, raw_row
FROM ingest_dlq_unresolved
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at)
ORDER BY occurred_at DESC
LIMIT 100

spec.title: Ingest DLQ row count
spec.description:
Goal: give the unresolved ingest_dlq dead-letter feed an at-a-glance signal that something still needs triage.
Description: counts ingest_dlq_unresolved rows (rejected agent_events/agent_usage/etc. inserts not yet marked resolved) in the selected time range - any non-zero value means unreplayed failures still need attention.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count() AS dlq_count
FROM ingest_dlq_unresolved
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at)

spec.title: Redis: Evicted keys/s
spec.description:
Goal: surface Redis key eviction pressure alongside the other at-a-glance health stats on the General tab.
Description: rate of redis_evicted_keys_total over a 5m window, an instant value - non-zero means Redis is evicting keys under memory pressure.

spec.title: Infra Overview
